title: Shimon ben Gurion
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot, at the supplied locator מפ״ה [compare the end of chapter 5], relates that the sages allotted Miriam, daughter of Shimon ben Gurion, five hundred dinars for a basket of perfumes. Ketubot 66b relates the incident about Nakdimon ben Gurion’s daughter.
Hyman adds that he was also called Buni, citing Taanit 20a.

notes.text: The Jerusalem Talmud locator מפ״ה is not securely resolved. The notice contrasts Shimon ben Gurion’s daughter with the Bavli’s Nakdimon ben Gurion daughter; it also calls the person Buni.

The saved whole Guggenheimer Ketubot5 final-halakhah scalar explicitly names Miriam daughter of Shimon benGurion and five hundred dinars for a perfume basket every day. This supports a matching end-of-chapter5 location alongside supplied מפ״ה, not a proven mem/samekh glyph error. Daily occurs in the witness but is absent from Hyman’s short notice and is not imported into its body. The Bavli Nakdimon comparison and Buni name remain Hyman’s comparisons, not an admitted identity equation; neither the Ketubot66b nor Taanit20a passage was newly read here.

Hyman’s print reads “end of chapter 5” (ספ״ה), where the supplied transcription reads מפ״ה. Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 5:11 allots Miriam, Shimon ben Gurion’s daughter, five hundred denars for perfume each day. Ketubot 66b allots the daughter of Nakdimon ben Gurion four hundred gold coins for perfume on that day. Taanit 20a explicitly calls Nakdimon Buni. These readings explain the comparison and leave the identity of the two men open.
